about: Conformance cases for the postprocess layer: five ports must reach the same
verdict on the same tokens. Every case is a regression from the shipped
reader (LoudReaderTests/TrailingFillerTests.swift) or a device trace named
in docs/postprocess.md — none was invented to exercise a branch.
Token sequences are written as a shape rather than spelled out, so the
intent stays readable. Build one by concatenating segments in order:
['speech', n] -> n tokens, the i-th being 20 + (i mod 60)
['quiet',  n] -> n tokens, the i-th being      (i mod 8)
The index restarts at 0 for every segment. Silence ids are 0..7, so 'quiet'
is silence and 'speech' never is.

ceiling.name: short text still gets the slack
ceiling.why: a ratio alone is unsafe on a three-word line; the slack carries it

ceiling.name: the showcase overrun
ceiling.why: device trace t3.overrun gen=92 ceiling=92 bestEOS=74@0.003 floor=31

ceiling.name: a long text is clamped to the window
ceiling.why: the renderer accepts 255 and the ceiling must never promise more. This expected 270 while saying exactly that: the +15 slack was unreachable, so a row was allowed to reach 270, stopped there, and then rejected at 255 — time spent on a device for tokens certain to be discarded.

trailing_filler.name: a long silence with a stray word is filler
trailing_filler.why: the case the rule exists for: sentence ends, silence, one word seconds later

trailing_filler.name: a tail that is still speech is not filler
trailing_filler.why: the model hesitated early; cutting here would drop 140 tokens of speech

trailing_filler.name: a pause followed by more sentence is not filler
trailing_filler.why: a rhetorical pause mid-tail was mistaken for the end of the sentence

trailing_filler.name: an empty tail is never filler
trailing_filler.why: nothing to discard is not a reason to cut

trailing_filler.name: an out-of-range index is never filler
an empty row is never filler
trailing_filler.why: index 0 into no tokens must not read past the end

desperation.name: an impossibly long row is cut at its seam
desperation.why: the 'Tas shape: real sentence, long silence seam, dense babble after

desperation.name: an impossibly long row without a seam is cut at the peak
desperation.why: 'It was as he expected.' — 14 text tokens, 96 speech tokens of dense babble

desperation.name: a peak outside the plausible band is not trusted
desperation.why: a peak that late is part of the garbage, not a stop

desperation.name: a merely slow row is never desperation cut
desperation.why: the mislabeled-language showcase row, 92 gen / 26 text = 3.5x

desperation.name: a tiny text is exempt from the ratio guard

desperation.name: nothing before the floor anchors a cut
desperation.why: a run straddling the floor belongs to the sentence; a peak below it is the old truncation bug

desperation.name: a continuation chunk never falls back to its peak
desperation.why: a chunk with no sentence end has no meaningful stop peak

ended_tail.name: a silence run with a blip before the stop is trimmed
ended_tail.why: the 'Tas device specimen ended '.......#' — seven silence tokens and a click

ended_tail.name: a short natural pause before the stop is left alone
ended_tail.why: three tokens of silence is no evidence of stranding

ended_tail.name: a bare long silence tail is tightened
ended_tail.why: dead air past half a second becomes a natural pause

ended_tail.name: a real trailing word is never trimmed mid-sentence
ended_tail.why: on a continuation chunk the pause is the sentence's rhythm

ended_tail.name: a stranded word behind a full seam is trimmed on a terminal chunk
ended_tail.why: heard live on the smoke's spoken proof: end, half a second, one word, stop

ended_tail.name: a word after a short pause is kept even terminally
ended_tail.why: that is the sentence's own ending cadence

ended_tail.name: a stranded word with trailing silence is still caught
ended_tail.why: a word wrapped in silence on both sides is junk; the click rule generalised

ended_tail.name: an all-silence row is left alone
ended_tail.why: there is no sentence to strand anything behind; walking back must stop

terminal_echo.name: the James device regression
terminal_echo.why: '...but a brigand. Pass. Four.' gen=124/124, bestEOS=109@0.004, ceiling hit

terminal_echo.name: a weak late peak without a ceiling overrun is refused
terminal_echo.why: weak confidence is trustworthy only with all three corroborators

terminal_echo.name: a strong late peak with a short tail is cut
terminal_echo.why: the ordinary echo: the sentence ended and one word free-ran after it

terminal_echo.name: a strong peak too early is a clause pause
terminal_echo.why: the late-position rule is what protects real comma and clause pauses

terminal_echo.name: a continuation chunk is never echo-cut
terminal_echo.why: its end is not an end

resolve.name: clean row passes through
resolve.why: a sentence that ended when it meant to keeps every token

resolve.name: silence tail wins over everything below it
resolve.why: the peak-anchored rescue is consulted first on a row that never stopped

resolve.name: a weak peak leaves the silence tail rule dormant
resolve.why: below filler_min_eos_probability the share test is not even consulted

resolve.name: desperation catches an ended row that babbled first
resolve.why: a model that babbles past its sentence and only then stops has forfeited that trust

resolve.name: ended tail trim only runs when nothing above fired
resolve.why: an ended row keeps its own decision; only stranded dead air comes off

resolve.name: an impossibly long row no rule can place is reported, not cut
resolve.why: cutting at a guess is how the rescue truncated whole sentences before

resolve.name: mode off returns the row untouched
resolve.why: the detectors cost an exponential per step; off must cost nothing and change nothing

about: Does the English-tuned ceiling truncate correct speech in the other
eight languages? Measured with one voice held constant across nine
language tags (voice-to-voice spread is larger than language-to-language,
so mixing voices would confound the effect), three length classes each.
Result: mid and long sentences run 1.69-2.79 speech tokens per text token
in every language, against a ceiling that only bites at 4.0 plus 40 slack.
The one row the ceiling stopped is a Spanish three-word phrase whose
decoder never emitted a stop token — a runaway the guard caught, not a
legitimate read it cut.
A port asserts ceiling_for() against `expect`, and that a row's measured
length is under that ceiling unless `expect_stopped_by_ceiling`.

repetition.name: a locked decoder repeating one token
repetition.why: VALL-E's greedy failure: the model 'continually generates' one code

repetition.name: a locked decoder repeating a short fragment
repetition.why: the common shape: a syllable-sized cycle read back off its own tail

repetition.name: a short repeat is how this model winds down
repetition.why: measured: healthy rows repeat a tail token for up to 10 tokens; keying on cycle count alone fired on 22 of 27 real renders

repetition.name: three repetitions of a word are speech, not a loop
repetition.why: 'very, very, very good' is a sentence; span and count both fall short

repetition.name: a long repeated block is rhetoric, not a lock
repetition.why: a repeated phrase is a refrain; only sub-half-second cycles count

repetition.name: a silence run is never a loop
repetition.why: the Spanish runaway repeats one silence token 44 times — a pause, not a lock-up, and the desperation rule already owns that row

repetition.name: a word-then-pause stutter is a loop
repetition.why: a cycle mixing silence with speech is still a stuck decoder

repetition.name: ordinary speech never anchors
repetition.why: the rule must be silent on a clean row, which is every row measured

repetition.name: a row too short to hold a qualifying span
repetition.why: no reading past the end on a two-token row

repetition_about: Extra shape segments used only here:
['cycle', p, k]        -> k copies of a p-token speech cycle (ids 20+i)
['cycle_mixed', p, k]  -> k copies of a p-token cycle whose second half
is silence, i.e. the word-then-pause stutter

about: Early truncation: the row is too short to be the text it was asked for.
Reported, never cut — there is nothing to cut. It is the only verdict here
that says 'what you have is incomplete' rather than 'the end of what you
have is wrong', and it is the most damaging failure in the set because a
listener cannot hear that anything is absent.
The floor is 25 speech tokens, borrowed from the published criterion for a
catastrophic neural-codec TTS failure rather than guessed. It applies only
when the text asked for more than arrived: the shortest healthy reads
measured across nine languages run 35 tokens, so a short line is exempt.

about: Long-form drift: per-chunk pace (speech tokens / text tokens) against the
passage's own median. Report-only — a strange pace is evidence of
something without saying what. The median, not the mean, so one broken
chunk cannot drag the baseline toward itself and hide. Tolerance 1.6x is
calibrated from the nine-language probe: healthy ratios run 1.69-2.79
across languages, so a chunk drifting 1.6x from its own passage's median
is outside anything ordinary prose produced.

cases.name: a healthy passage flags nothing
cases.why: the common case must stay silent

cases.name: a dragging chunk is flagged
cases.why: 5.9 against a median of 2.2 is the runaway shape, mid-passage

cases.name: a rushing chunk is flagged
cases.why: 0.9 against 2.2 is the truncation shape: less speech than text

cases.name: two chunks cannot accuse each other
cases.why: with no third opinion, which one drifted is unknowable

cases.name: a broken chunk cannot hide by dragging the mean
cases.why: median baseline: two bad chunks among five still both flag
